summary: Godot reports a broken resource reference only when that scene loads, often in an exported build on another machine. godot-refcheck reads the project files instead: missing paths, case-only differences that break outside Windows, unknown and duplicated uid://, undeclared ExtResource ids, stale .import metadata.
key_features: Eight checks over .tscn, .tres, project.godot, .import, plugin.cfg, GDScript and shaders, in both the Godot 3 and Godot 4 formats
Every check is compared with a real headless Godot by tools/verify_with_godot.py; six have a matching engine message and the other two are documented as static-only
Calibrated against 237 projects in eleven real repositories: 25 findings, each confirmed by hand, and nothing else reported
Text, JSON and SARIF 2.1.0 output, plus a composite GitHub Action that puts findings on the changed lines of a pull request

social.headline: Godot only tells you a reference is broken when that scene loads. godot-refcheck tells you at commit time.

provenance.rule: mechanical fields read from the repository; counts taken from a run recorded in CI; no field is generated from a guess
